dedupe_keys.name: reform d1 4 inventory of river restoration measures effects costs and benefits

description: This REFORM deliverable reviews the costs and benefits of river restoration in Europe and assembles a database of restoration measure costs to study them empirically. It was written by Andrew Ayres, Holger Gerdes, Brandon Goeller and Manuel Lago of Ecologic with co-authors from CEDEX, IVM Amsterdam and the University of Hull, for the EU FP7 project REFORM (Restoring rivers for effective catchment management, grant 282656), and submitted in January 2014. It summarises restoration planning and individual measures, reviews peer-reviewed and technical literature on their effects, and reviews valuation studies of benefits to households, as a basis for later cost-benefit analysis. Coverage is European rivers. Format and access: a public 96-page PDF deliverable. Licence: not stated; free. Caveats: the review is non-exhaustive, the cost database itself is summarised, not released as a file, and the authors stress that effects of measures are hard to predict at European scale. It supports appraisal of river restoration as green-blue flood and water infrastructure. Related catalogue records are the Lower Danube Green Corridor case study and the Isar-Plan river restoration in Munich.
